q: 1. Lime is mixed with brick earth
explain: Lime in brick earth helps the silica to fuse at a lower temperature and prevents the raw bricks from shrinking and warping.

q: 2. The crushing strength of 1st class brick should not be less than
explain: 1st class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive (crushing) strength of 10.5 N/mm² or 105 kg/cm².

q: 3. For one cubic meter of brick masonry, the number of machine made brick required as per NS is
explain: According to Nepal Standards, approximately 530 machine-made bricks are required to complete 1 cubic meter of masonry.

q: 4. The number of standard bricks required for one cubic meter of brick masonry (IS standard) is
explain: For standard modular bricks (19cm x 9cm x 9cm), the nominal requirement including mortar is 500 bricks per cubic meter.

q: 5. The percentage of alumina in a good brick clay should vary from .....
explain: Good brick earth contains about 20 to 30% alumina, which gives plasticity.

q: 6. The soil used for the manufacture of bricks should preferably not contain the following material
explain: Pebbles and stones prevent the uniform mixing of clay and can cause the brick to crack during the burning process.

q: 7. Tiles are used for
explain: Clay tiles are versatile components used for roofing, flooring, and constructing drainage conduits.

q: 8. The amount of local brick required for one m3 masonry (As per NS norms)
explain: Due to size variations in local traditional bricks in Nepal, the norm usually estimates 560 bricks per cubic meter.

q: 9. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: smaller than the size of fully burnt brick
larger than the size of fully burnt brick
equal to the size of fully burnt brick
explain: Moulds are made 8-10% larger than the desired brick size to account for the shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.

q: 10. The density of common bricks varies from
explain: Common clay bricks typically have a density ranging from about 1600 to 1920 kg/m3.

q: 11. Pug mill is used for
explain: A pug mill is used for 'pugging,' which is the process of kneading the clay to make it uniform and plastic for moulding.

q: 12. The ingredient of the brick earth which enables the brick to retain shape is
explain: Alumina imparts plasticity to clay, allowing the brick to be molded and retain its shape.

q: 13. Advantage of clamp burning as compared to kiln burning is
options: when large number of bricks are required
explain: Clamps are temporary structures and do not require the expensive permanent construction associated with kilns.

q: 14. Percentage to silica in a good brick earth lies between
explain: Good brick earth typically contains about 50-60% silica, providing the main structural bulk of the clay.

q: 15. The over ground continuous kiln is
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a permanent, over-ground continuous kiln, whereas Bull's Trench is typically partially underground.

q: 16. The type of glass used to make laboratory equipment and cooking utensils is .....
explain: Borosilicate glass has high heat and chemical resistance, so it is used for lab ware and cookware.

q: 17. Excess of silica in brick earth causes
explain: Excess silica reduces the clay's plasticity and binding capacity, causing loss of cohesion and brittle, weak bricks.

q: 18. Hoffman's kiln is a
explain: Hoffman's kilns allow for continuous loading, burning, and unloading of bricks in different chambers simultaneously.

q: 19. Water glass is .....
options: water formed by condensation on glass
solution of sodium silicate in water
explain: Water glass is a solution of sodium silicate in water.

q: 20. Which brick is adopted well ?
explain: A high-quality brick must possess all these physical characteristics: high strength, proper burning, and low porosity.

q: 21. The bricks used for lining of furnaces is
explain: Refractory (fire) bricks are specifically made to withstand the intense heat inside furnaces and chimneys.

q: 22. The over ground continuous kiln is called
explain: A tunnel kiln is built above ground and operates continuously as bricks move through it on trolleys.

q: 23. Fire bricks should be laid in a
explain: To maintain thermal consistency, fire bricks are laid using fire clay mortar which can resist similar high temperatures.

q: 24. The bricks used for lining of furnaces are
explain: Refractory bricks, made to withstand very high temperatures, are used to line furnaces.

q: 25. In bricks masonry, the frog of the brick generally kept on
explain: The 'frog' (indentation) is placed facing up so that it can be filled with mortar, creating a mechanical key with the course above.

q: 26. If iron oxide present in brick earth is more than the requirement then colour of the brick after burning will be
explain: Excess iron oxide oxidizes further during burning, deepening the red color of the fired brick.

q: 27. Bull nose bricks are not used in
explain: Bullnose bricks have rounded edges and are used for corners or pillars, but they are not standard for arch construction.

q: 28. Hollow bricks are used for
explain: The air trapped inside hollow bricks acts as an excellent thermal insulator, keeping interiors cooler in summer and warmer in winter.

q: 29. Fire bricks are used
explain: Refractory bricks have low thermal conductivity, helping to contain heat within a furnace and decrease outward heat flow.

q: 30. Terracotta is used in building for
explain: Terracotta is a glazed or unglazed fired clay used primarily for decorative architectural elements and ornamental work.

q: 31. Bloating of bricks is due to
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter and sulphur
presence of any gas forming material in clay
explain: Bloating is a spongy swollen mass caused by the entrapped gases from carbonaceous matter and sulphur during firing.

q: 32. Swelling of bricks is known as
explain: Bloating is the term for the permanent swelling of a brick, often caused by internal gas pressure during burning.

q: 33. The quantity of sand in brick is about
explain: Silica (sand) typically makes up about 50-60% of brick earth, which is roughly equivalent to 3/5ths.

q: 34. The bricks are properly soaked in water before use the following reason
options: to wash the kiln dust for better bondage with mortar
to avoid the chances of absorption of water from the mortar
to spread the mortar uniformly between them
explain: Soaking ensures the bricks don't suck water from the mortar (which weakens it) and removes dust for better adhesion.

q: 35. In one day, the height of brick masonry construction should generally not exceed
explain: To prevent the fresh mortar in lower courses from being crushed by the weight of new work, the daily height is limited to 1m.

q: 36. Frog means
explain: In masonry terminology, a frog is the depression or indentation made on the top face of a brick.

q: 37. For manufacture of bricks normally the top soil is removed having a depth of .....
explain: The top 20cm of soil is usually stripped away (unsoiling) as it contains organic matter and impurities unsuitable for bricks.

q: 38. Tampering of soil for manufacture of bricks, is done by
explain: Kneading the soil (tempering) can be done manually by feet, using cattle, or mechanically in a pug mill.

q: 39. In case of clamp for burning of bricks, the bricks/ fuel are laid at a slope of...
explain: Clamps are constructed with a slight inward slope, usually around 15 degrees, to ensure stability as the fuel burns away.

q: 40. Normally the bricks (1st class) obtained from pazawah is about
explain: Pazawah (clamp) burning is less efficient than kiln burning, typically yielding about 60% good quality bricks.

q: 41. Terracotta, in building, is used for
explain: Terracotta, a fired clay product, is commonly used for decorative and ornamental architectural work.

q: 42. Lamination of bricks is caused due to
options: entrapped air in the voids of the clay
entrapped water in the voids of the clay
explain: Lamination occurs when air is trapped within the clay during machine moulding, creating thin layers or planes of weakness.

q: 43. Strike is used to remove the
explain: A strike is a wooden or metal straight-edge used to scrape off excess clay from the top of the mould.

q: 44. The glass used for security purpose is .....
explain: Bullet proof glass is used where security is required.

q: 45. Glazing of clay products, is done .....
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing improves appearance, makes the product impervious and protects it from weather and corrosive action.

q: 46. Refractory bricks are
explain: Refractory bricks are categorized into three types—acidic, basic, and neutral—based on their chemical resistance to slag.

q: 47. A pug mill is used for .....
explain: A pug mill is used for tempering (thoroughly mixing) brick earth with water.

q: 48. Generally wooden moulds are made from
explain: Hardwoods like Shisham are preferred for brick moulds because they resist wear and warping from moisture.

q: 49. Choose the correct statement
options: percentage of silica is increased in 1st class brick
percentage of alumina is increased in refractory brick
percentage of alumina is increased in 1st class brick
explain: Refractory bricks require a higher percentage of alumina (and silica) to withstand extreme temperatures without melting.

q: 50. If rain water falls on hot bricks then the shape of the brick gets deformed, this defect is known as
explain: Chuffs is the defect caused when falling rain hits hot, newly burnt bricks, resulting in cracking and deformation.
